messages.author: c93b61679b5dd671
messages.subject: Re: Error in the normalize2
parts:
Dear Adam,

Thanks for spotting this out and offering the solution! It sounds good to me! Just to make sure, are all of your samples processed in a same batch by the same capture design? CODEX estimates the exon-wise latent factor using normal sample only. Although we don’t require matched tumor normal samples, we normally feed the program with relative large number of samples so the estimation is more accurate. With only one sample, at most one latent artifact can be removed and I feel this might be a bit risky. With this said, you can give it a try and see if the results make sense. Also, if you are interested in finding rare copy number variants (compared to common patterns across all tumors), you can also use normalize() by throwing in all the samples for normalization.

I am cc’ing the mailing list of our user group just so if people using the software have similar questions.

Let me know if you have further questions!

Yuchao




On Apr 30, 2015, at 12:13 PM, Adam Rabinowitz <Adam.Ra...@crick.ac.uk> wrote:

Dear Yuchao,
 
I have been working with your package CODEX to analyse exome data. I am grateful for your work in developing such a useful package. I think I have found a very minor bug that may need addressing.
 
Within my experiment I have four tumour samples and a case-control sample. I therefore have been using the normalize2 function to normalise the tumour data to the case-control. When using the normalise2 function I receive the following error message:
 
Error in apply((Y_qc/(fhatnew * Nmat * exp(ghat %*% t(hhat))))[, normal_index],  :
  dim(X) must have a positive length
 
I have traced the error message to following line in the normalize2 function:
 
betahatnew = apply((Y_qc/(fhatnew * Nmat * exp(ghat %*% 
                                                       t(hhat))))[, normal_index], 1, median)
 
When a single case-control sample is present then the Y_qc matrix is sliced with a single index and converted into a vector. By adding ‘drop=F’ into the code the error is avoided and the data is normalised without any further error messages. The modified line of code is as follows.
 
betahatnew = apply((Y_qc/(fhatnew * Nmat * exp(ghat %*% 
                                                       t(hhat))))[, normal_index,drop=F], 1, median)
 
I would be grateful if you would confirm that my alteration is effective. Thanks again for developing the software.
 
Best wishes,
 
Adam Rabinowitz

1)      Do I need to alter other portions of the code, in addition to ‘getcg’ and ‘getmapp’ to make CODEX compatible with mouse exome data?

2)      What software package and parameters did you use to compute mappability scores?

 

Thanks for your help

 

Adam

messages.subject: RE: Error in the normalize2
parts:
Hi Adam,

 

Yes, the rest parts should work the same as homo sapiens. I am glad that you modified getgc() to get the gc content – this is very crucial for normalization. The mappability is used in the QC procedure to filter out exons that are hard to map. I have codes for the computation of mappability (outlined below from CODEX’s online supplements) however they tend to be very computationally intensive. Therefore, I precompute the mappabilities for hg19 exons and stored the quantities in the package.

 

To calculate the exonic mappability, we first construct consecutive reads that are one base pair (bp) apart along the exon. The length of the reads is set to be the same as that from the sequencing technology and the sequences are taken from the hg19 reference. We then find possible positions across the genome that the reads can map to allowing for a default number of mismatches (2 for the 1000 Genomes Project data set in our study which has read 100). Finally we compute the mean of the probabilities that the overlapped reads map to the target places where they are generated and use this as the mappability of the exon.

I would suggest you either get the mappability from online database (I know for hg19 one can download the mappabilities from the UCSC genome browser) or just exclude this mappability QC. If you are interested in getting the codes, however, let me know and I will try to send them to you after my finals (next week).

 

Cheers,

Yuchao
